newsitem.title: USA: Envoy asks U.S. to help unify, demilitarize Cyprus.
newsitem.headline: Envoy asks U.S. to help unify, demilitarize Cyprus.

text.p: The Cypriot ambassador to the United States, Andreas Jacovides, urged President Bill Clinton on Sunday to use U.S. influence to achieve a united, demilitarized Cyprus.

"We sincerely appreciate President Clinton's repeated expressions of interest for progress on the Cyprus problem," Jacovides told about 300 members of the Greek community and guests, including Delaware Sen. Joseph Biden, a ranking member of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee.
Jacovides said there were still 35,000 Turkish troops on Cyprus despite resolutions by Congress supporting demilitarization.

The eastern Mediterranean island has been divided since Turkey invaded the northern third in 1974 after a brief coup engineered by the colonels ruling Greece at the time. Turkey declared a breakaway Turkish Cypriot state in 1983, but it is recognised only by Ankara.
Along with the Turkish troops, there are 1,200 United Nations peacekeepers on Cyprus and the 10,000-strong Greek Cypriot National Guard.
Cyprus is known as a listening post for international intelligence services in the region and is used as a flyover base for U.S. Middle East surveillance.

Jacovides wants all troops removed from Cyprus except for the U.N. peacekeepers, integration of the Turkish and Greek communities into a single federation and, ultimately, the admission of Cyprus into the European Union.
Biden could not be reached for comment.
